Protagonist

/pruh-TAG-uh-nist/ — stress on 'TAG' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

The protagonist of a story is its main character, the one whose goals and actions drive the plot forward.

The protagonist of the series is a shy mapmaker who becomes an explorer.

Worked Example

The protagonist of the fantasy series is a resourceful scavenger who must discover the truth about her past and save her world.

Protagonist is precise because it specifically names the main character whose goals and actions drive the story forward—not just any important character, but the central one whose journey the reader follows. It's more exact than 'main character' and more specific than 'character.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hero: a main character admired for bravery or goodness

main character: the central figure a story follows

lead: the most important role in a performance

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

antagonist: the character who opposes the main character

bystander: someone who watches without taking part

Where it sits · how central to the story's action — witness → ally → antagonist → protagonist

witness vs. protagonist: A witness is far less central than a protagonist: a witness merely observes events, while the protagonist is the character whose goals and actions drive the entire story.

ally vs. protagonist: An ally is closer to the action than a witness but still weaker than a protagonist: an ally helps the main character, while the protagonist carries the plot itself.

antagonist vs. protagonist: An antagonist matches the protagonist in importance but from the opposite side: the protagonist pushes the story's goal forward, while the antagonist works to block it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — prot- / proto-

Prefix — prot- / proto-: first (Greek)

Root — agonist (from agon)

Root — agonist (from agon): actor, competitor; contest (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Prot- ('first') + agonist ('actor, competitor') literally names the 'first actor' — in Greek drama, the performer who played the chief part. Today the protagonist is a story's main character, the one whose goals and actions drive the plot forward.

Use the root in a new word: prototype

Use the root in a new word: prototype: Engineers built a prototype, the first working model of the car — the same Greek proto- ('first') that makes the protagonist a story's first, leading character.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Protagonist is the precise literary term for the main character whose goals and actions drive the plot. 'Main character' works in casual talk, but protagonist is the term to use in essays about literature. Every story has a protagonist—the character whose journey matters most.
